conviction_note: This print turns on the capital structure, not the quarter. About $558m of debt is due 22 Dec 2026 and the 10-K carries a going-concern doubt. The Aurelius sale missed its 12 Oct condition. Bloomberg said a Chapter 11 filing could come as soon as November. On 11 Oct the board added a restructuring professional on a $30k-a-month fee and put him on the Strategy Committee. So the 9 Nov release, with a webcast presentation, is the first scheduled update, and it is close to binary: a filing or an RSA that wipes out equity (about -50 to -75%), an extension with the sale closing (about +80% or more), or 'talks continue' (about -5 to -15%). abs_move_pct is 28, above the 12.15 median reaction because the outcome is binary and 20-day realised vol is 216%. p_up is 40, a lean down that rests on the 8-K director appointment and the going-concern state. The -51% day on 15 Oct has already priced most of the bankruptcy risk: a $12.7m market cap against about $500m of net debt, so the lean stays mild. The findings sum (-6.0) and the scaled number (-5.6) happen to agree; neither was fitted to the other.
bar: unsourced. I found no consensus revenue or EPS for fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026) in two agreeing sources, and the company gave no FY27 guidance in the Q4 FY26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910406/000119312526389814/hain-ex99_1.htm). The only sell-side datum found was Barclays at Underweight with a $0.30 target, cut from $0.50, quoted in an aggregator snippet. The bar the market is really holding is a capital-structure update: is the 22 Dec maturity extended or is there a filing? The Q1 operating numbers are secondary. Every quarter-based finding is therefore capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest was 5.24m shares at the 15 Oct 2026 settlement with 2.8 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/hain, the source the search returned; the same page shows plausible late-October prices). That is about 5.8% of the 91.0m shares outstanding, so the short is not crowded. Earlier readings were higher: 12.5m, 13.9% of float, 12.1 days at 15 Apr 2026 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/the-hain-celestial-group-inc-nasdaqhain-sees-large-increase-in-short-interest-2026-05-01/), so shorts covered heavily into and after the collapse. Holder base: after the crash two non-institutional 13G filers crossed 5%. Ganesh Goroba Yadav holds 7.6% (event 20 Oct, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910406/000216224526000001/primary_doc.xml) and Ng Chee Tat Philip's entities hold 5.5% (event 16 Oct, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910406/000107997326001393/primary_doc.xml), so the holder base is now retail and speculative. Options: chain unusable, no skew; put/call OI is 0.14 on 4,108 contracts, call-heavy. Tape: $0.1397, -74.6% over 20 days, +16.4% over 5 days off the $0.12 low of 29-30 Oct. Turnover is about $0.2-0.3m a day on 0.6-2.7m shares.

findings.finding: 8-K of 15 Oct: on 11 Oct 2026 the board appointed Richard Shinder and Patricia Ferrari as directors at a $30,000 monthly cash fee each, both on the Strategy Committee, as two directors resigned. Shinder is a restructuring banker (ex-Blackstone restructuring and Perella Weinberg partner, founder of the fiduciary-services firm Theatine Partners and of the debt-restructuring boutique Ensis Partners, launched Feb 2026). A monthly-fee restructuring director on a strategy committee is the standard governance step before a court-supervised or lender-led restructuring, and it points to the 9 Nov release carrying an RSA or filing more than an extension. Bar: the market holds roughly 'Chapter 11 likely' (stock -51% on 15 Oct), so this sharpens a lean rather than reversing it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The capital-structure line has moved this stock far more than the quarter. On 15 Oct 2026 the 8-K disclosing the missed lender condition plus the Bloomberg Chapter 11 report took it -51% ($0.58 to $0.28 on 10.8m shares). On 14 Sep 2026 the sale announcement with Q4 moved it only -3.23%. On 7 May 2025 it fell -47.65% on a print. Source for the October prices: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/hain/history/
findings.why_not_priced: The crash on 15 Oct was a reaction to the missed deadline and the Bloomberg report. The board appointment sat in the same 8-K under item 5.02, and the wire summaries I found (Bloomberg via Yahoo, Securitas, Food Institute) do not mention Shinder's restructuring background. If the market had priced a near-certain in-court wipe-out, the stock would trade at the $0.02-0.05 level of a post-filing equity rather than at $0.14, and it would not have bounced 16% in five days.
findings.independence: Shinder's background comes from a different source: Ensis Partners launch, Business Wire 2026-02-02 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260202825274/en) and Piper Jaffray hire release (https://pipersandler.com/news/piper-jaffray-adds-industry-veteran-richard-shinder-its-capital-advisory-group). The 'as soon as November' Chapter 11 timing is a separate Bloomberg report (finding 2). The reading of the appointment is an inference: no document says a filing is planned.

findings.finding: The maturity wall is 43 days past the print and the condition that solved it failed. Per the 15 Oct 8-K, the credit-agreement amendment the Aurelius sale needed by 12 Oct 'was not satisfied', and the company is still 'in discussions with its lenders regarding its capital structure'. Debt was $557.6m, almost all current, maturing 22 Dec 2026, against $58m of cash and net secured leverage of 4.5x. The FY26 10-K carries substantial doubt about going concern, and the amendment needs every lender's consent. Bloomberg (15 Oct) reported the company could seek Chapter 11 'as soon as next month'. The 9 Nov release is the first scheduled update since then and must address this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the same line as finding 1 and the 15 Oct -51% day. The 14 Sep release, which carried the sale and the 'lender extension assumed' outlook, moved -3.23%.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of this is priced, by the -51% day and the drift from $0.28 to $0.14. What is not priced is the timing: November was Bloomberg's earliest date and the release is in November. A $12.7m equity value is still about 2.5% of net debt, which is option value for an out-of-court extension that this finding argues is less likely. Fully priced would look like the stock trading at post-filing levels.
findings.independence: Bloomberg via Yahoo, 15 Oct 2026 (https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/hain-celestial-weighs-chapter-11-211612563.html), is a separate source for the Chapter 11 timing. The debt figures are from the Q4 FY26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910406/000119312526389814/hain-ex99_1.htm), and the going-concern and all-lender-consent points from https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/hain-celestial-hain-signs-323m-203013194.html. This shares the 15 Oct 8-K with finding 1, but they rest on different items (8.01 here, 5.02 there).

findings.finding: The upside path is real and documented. Lenders have granted Hain relief (waivers, extra debt room, repricing) six times since 2016, and on 2 Oct 2026 an independent analysis called an extension, clean or with a sale deadline, more likely than a default. The 15 Oct 8-K also says the company is still talking with AURELIUS and 'continues to pursue a path forward for completing the International Business Transaction'. If the 9 Nov release announces an amendment or extension plus the $305-310m of net sale proceeds, post-sale net debt is about $210m. That analysis put base-case equity near $1.10 a share, against $0.14 now.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 11 May 2026 a print with debt reduction and refinancing plans moved +10.61%. On 7 Nov 2025 a print moved +12.15%. With the equity now at $0.14, a credible extension would move it far more than either, which is the reason for the wide upper bound.
findings.why_not_priced: At $0.14 the market gives this path low odds. The analysis predates the missed 12 Oct deadline, which is why it is sized small. A market that believed it would hold the stock nearer the pre-miss $0.58.
findings.independence: The company's own 15 Oct 8-K language that sale talks continue (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910406/000119312526422226/hain-20261009.htm). The lender-relief history is the analyst's count, not a primary document.

findings.finding: The underlying business the lenders would keep is stable and cash-generative. In Q4 FY26 (to 30 Jun 2026) North America organic net sales grew +2% with $16m of adjusted EBITDA at a 14.4% margin. FY26 free cash flow was $58m and adjusted EBITDA $89m. So the fiscal Q1 operating numbers are unlikely to be the shock, and they support either a lender extension or a high-recovery prepack for lenders, though not necessarily for equity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 14 Sep 2026 the Q4 print plus the sale news moved -3.23%: operating numbers have not moved this stock lately next to the capital-structure news.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, or irrelevant to the equity. There is no consensus to beat, and the bar is unsourced, which caps this finding small.

findings.finding: The chief accounting officer, Michael Ragusa, gave notice on 25 Sep 2026 and left on 1 Nov 2026, eight days before the 10-Q for the quarter is due, with the CFO taking over as principal accounting officer. The accounting chair is empty as the first going-concern 10-Q is filed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none found for officer departures at HAIN
findings.why_not_priced: It was disclosed in a late 8-K item and drew no coverage I could find. Its only effect inside the window is as one more sign of an organisation preparing for a change of control, or a risk of a late 10-Q.
findings.independence: The Form 4s of 27 and 30 Oct show only Ragusa's routine RSU vesting with tax withholding at $0.13-0.15 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910406/000119312526441996/ownership.xml): no insider buying.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print skews retail and long. Two non-institutional holders crossed 5% after the crash (Yadav 7.6%, event 20 Oct; Ng Chee Tat Philip 5.5%, event 16 Oct). Short interest was about 5.8% of shares with 2.8 days to cover (15 Oct). Option OI is call-heavy (put/call 0.14). The stock bounced +16% in five days off the $0.12 low, with 2.7m shares traded on 2 Nov, the day the earnings date was set. That gives some squeeze fuel on a non-filing outcome and concentrated holders who may sell on a filing; on net it is close to neutral.
findings.why_not_priced: The holder base and the bounce are visible in the tape. This is a small item filed for the panel, not an edge.

outside_window.finding: Credit-agreement maturity on 22 Dec 2026, about $557.6m. A filing could come any time before it rather than with the 9 Nov release.
The Nasdaq minimum-bid cure period runs to 22 Mar 2027, after the transfer to the Capital Market on 24 Sep 2026; a reverse split is possible.

searched_and_found_nothing: Any 8-K, press release or credible report dated 3-6 Nov 2026 of a lender amendment, forbearance, RSA, Aurelius termination or Chapter 11 filing: nothing found. The last company update on the capital structure is the 15 Oct 8-K.
Patricia Ferrari's background: no restructuring-director record found

Scanner data for Celestial Seasonings, Earth's Best or Greek Gods: not searched in depth, because the operating quarter is secondary to the capital structure

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The 20-day run-up (-74.6%) already prices the negative state, and the +16% five-day bounce plus call-heavy OI lean the other way. My mild negative lean therefore runs against recent positioning and with the longer drawdown, and p_up sits only 10 points below 50 to reflect that.
lessons_applied: 'Two readings of one document / same event' and rule 3: the draft's separate 'missed 12 Oct condition' (-2.0) and 'Bloomberg Chapter 11 as soon as November' (-2.0) rest on one event and one priced day, so they are merged into one -3.0 financing finding.

Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the positive 'lender relief history' analysis predates the missed deadline, which its own why_not_priced concedes, so it is cut from +2.0 to +1.0 with the upper range kept wide.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): answered. The debt is not funding a ramp; it is a maturity wall with a going-concern flag, so the negative sign stands.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): no consensus found, so the reported-quarter finding stays capped at +0.5 and print_vs_bar_pct is null. The 22 Dec maturity and the Nasdaq cure date are kept in outside_window.

Rule 7 (short interest before a negative): checked. Short interest was about 5.8% with 2.8 days to cover, not crowded, so the negatives are not shrunk for squeeze risk; the retail-heavy holder base is filed as a positioning finding.
abs_move_pct (28) and p_up (40) unchanged by the file.
